title: Affine localization comparison for the injective restriction source
statement: Let $L$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $U$ an open subscheme, $N$ a quasi-coherent module [pqf-def-coherent], and $V$ an affine open. Write $R=\mathcal O_L(V)$ and $P=(j_*(N|_U))(V)$ for $j:U\hookrightarrow L$. Let $S\subseteq P$ be a finitely generated $R$-submodule and $p$ a prime ideal of $R$. Set $y=h_V.\mathrm{fromSpec}(p)$, the corresponding point of $V$. Assume N is finite on affine opens, its stalks outside U have depth at least two [def-weil-pbc-depth], and the restriction unit is injective on all opens. Write $a:N(V)\to P$ for this unit, assume $a(N(V))\subseteq S$, and let $K=a(N(V))\cap S$ viewed as a submodule of S. Then $K_p$ is finite over $R_p$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. If $y\in U$, then $(S/K)_p=0$. If $y\notin U$, then $\operatorname{depth}_{R_p}(K_p)\ge2$. No depth conclusion about $(S/K)_p$ at boundary points is asserted.

proof.text: Define M=N(V). Injectivity of a and the containment of its range in S give a linear equivalence M to K: m maps to a(m), with the S-membership witness from the containment; every k in K has an a-preimage and uniqueness follows from injectivity. Thus K is finite, and its localization is finite.

Let y be the affine point of p. The affine ring stalk comparison identifies R_p with O_L,y. The quasi-coherent affine module stalk presentation identifies M_p with N_y, with the germ scalar action. After localizing M to K, these identify K_p with N_y semilinearly over the ring isomorphism. Mapping regular sequences through the ring isomorphism preserves their membership in the maximal ideal, injective multiplication at each quotient, and quotient nontriviality; hence it preserves depth. The assumed boundary depth bound therefore gives depth(K_p) at least two.

At y in U the restriction unit is an isomorphism on stalks, as restriction followed by open direct image restricts back to the original sheaf. The qcqs direct image is quasi-coherent. Identify its affine prime localization with its stalk by the same affine presentation. Then the composite M_p to S_p to P_p is an isomorphism and both inclusions are injective, so K_p to S_p is surjective. Localization of K to S to S/K is exact; its localized cokernel is therefore zero. The map comparisons are the natural germ maps and localization maps, so the composite is the given unit map.
